title: View spec 1.0 (contract 1.8)
description: The declarative page that agents edit through ops (see ops.schema.json) and browsers render. Panels and marks carry queries on /insights (and /trends), never data: the renderer fetches, and every number on the page comes from the API. Contract 1.1 is additive: spec_version stays 1.0, so a 1.0 renderer still reads every 1.0 spec.

version.description: 0 is the baseline; every accepted batch, undo, redo or reset makes a new version.

message.description: The message of the batch that made this version, if any.

next_mark_n.description: The number the next mark gets. Mark numbers are monotonic and never reused; a mark's id is 'm' + its number.

next_story_n.description: Optional (contract 1.6): the page number the next new storyline gets. The backend keeps it and never lowers it, except when the page is reset or cleared (scope page), so a storyline keeps its number and a number is never given to another storyline.

agent_name.description: trend_finder, cause_finder, forecaster, visualizer, any registered agent, 'user' (the person at the page) or 'baseline' (version 0 only).

geo_code.description: A partner or reporter code: FR, CN, EU27_2020.

code.description: Any dimension code: a country (FR), a product (85, 8517, 85171300), OTHER.

context.description: What the page is about: the year (or month) and the goods the user's Year and Goods controls show, and (1.4) who it is read by. Panels follow it through the placeholders $period, $previous (the year before $period: 2025 -> 2024, 2025-03 -> 2024-03) and $product in their query params (1.4: $start, the first year of a range, in start). Changed with the set_context op. A spec without context reads as {period: 2025, product: TOTAL}.

product.description: TOTAL (all goods) or an HS code: 85, 8517, 85171300.

flow.description: Optional emphasis; BOTH (or absent) shows both flows.

start.description: Optional (contract 1.4): the first year of a range the page's totals sum over (the From control), up to the year in period (the To control). Panels follow it through the placeholder $start (in start). Absent, after period, or with a month as period: a single period, $start reads as period.

persona.description: Optional (contract 1.4): who the page is drawn for, the id of a persona profile in contract/personas/persona_profiles.json (statec_analyst, journalist, citizen...). It changes panels, wording and depth, never a figure. Absent: the page as it was before personas.

panel_context.description: Optional (contract 1.5): the panel's own year and goods, which win over the page context for this panel only: its queries, inline facts and the marks drawn on it fill $period, $previous, $start and $product from {...spec.context, ...panel.context}. A period without a start is a single period (start reads as period). Set with the set_panel_context op; absent: the panel follows the page.

start.description: The From year of a range, up to period (the To year).

product.description: TOTAL (all goods) or an HS code.

params.description: Query-string parameters: dimension filters (flow=EXPORT, partner=FR, product=85) and the endpoint's own parameters. Scalars only, so no data can travel in a spec. A value may be a context placeholder: $period or $previous (in period, previous, start, end, base), $start (1.4, in start: context.start, else the period) or $product (in product, parent); the renderer and the backend's pre-flight substitute it from spec.context.

tone.description: Data colour: exports sky blue, imports steel grey. Agent colours are for marks only.

key.description: Name of the query inside its panel (imports, exports, in, out, main). Marks refer to it as 'series', facts as 'query'.

path.description: Where a value sits in an API response, as dot-separated segments: a key (total), an index (0, -1 from the end), [field=value] (the first array item whose field equals value, e.g. [code=FR]), #length (array length) and #position (1-based position of the item just selected by [field=value]). Examples: total, n_items, items.[code=CN].value, -1.value, [is_focus=true].#position, peers.#length.

format.description: eur: 25097941118 -> €25.1 bn, 613389780 -> €613 m. pct: a fraction (0.875 -> 87%). percent: already in percent (5.5 -> 5.5%). *_signed adds + or −. ordinal: 27 -> 27th. text: as is (a name). 1.8, quantities (a query with measure weight, units or all): qty, a count (37654 -> 37,654); qty:<unit>, the count and its unit (qty:cars -> 37,654 cars); tonnes (122464.3 -> 122,464 t).

fact.description: A number (or name) the renderer resolves from the API and puts where {name} appears in a text. Three forms: from one of the panel's own queries {query, path}; from an inline query {endpoint, params, path} (marks have no queries of their own); derived from other facts {op, of}.

op.description: diff a-b, sum a+b, ratio a/b, growth a/b-1, abs |a|.

template.description: Prose with {fact} placeholders. Figures (amounts, percentages) must come from facts, never be typed in; years and codes may be written.

url.description: An API call relative to the backend (/insights/ranking?by=partner&...) or another source (a URL, a file in the repo).

provenance.description: Who made it and from what. In ops every field is optional: the backend fills agent, run_id and created_at and appends the URL of every query it pre-flighted to sources.

panel_type.description: 1.0: kpi, bar, line, table, flow, text. 1.1: waterfall (main: /insights/movers), choropleth (main: /insights/ranking by partner, or /insights/flows for measure balance), flowmap (main: /insights/flows), heatmap (main: /insights/series freq M, /insights/matrix or /trends/seasonal-heatmap, by options.kind; analysis?: /trends/analyze, for facts),treemap (main: /insights/tree), butterfly (in and out: /insights/ranking), bump (main: /insights/matrix measure rank), scatter (main: /insights/specialisation, growth?: /insights/movers or /insights/trends). 1.2: compare, either 1 to 6 series over time (every query on /insights/series, one per partner, product or reporter; the key names the series and the label is its direct label) or two snapshots side by side (queries a and b on the same /insights/ranking or /insights/compare, e.g. two years), drawn in options.compare mode.

compare_mode.description: How a comparison is drawn. absolute: the values. index: each series rebased to 100 at options.base_period (default: the first period they share). share: each series as a share of options.reference (a query key, e.g. the world total), or of the sum of the series shown. yoy: growth against the previous period (the same month a year earlier for monthly series); on two snapshots, the growth from a to b. diff: each series minus options.reference (a query key); on two snapshots, b minus a. There is no per-capita mode: the data has no population source.

text.description: kpi: the caption under the figure. text: the body (rendered in the serif). Others: a caption under the chart.

value.description: kpi only: the fact shown as the big figure.

pinned.description: Pinned panels survive clear and cannot be removed.

agent.description: Who created the panel; 'baseline' for the panels of version 0.

measure.description: Contract 1.7: growth draws each item's growth per year over a span (the compound annual growth of /insights/trends, query main), sorted, with its first and last value; the query needs start.

compare_options.description: The comparison options of a compare panel, also accepted by a line (series over time). A bar takes compare, sort and focus for two snapshots a and b.

base_period.description: index: the period every series is 100 at. Default: the first period the series share.

reference.description: share: the query everything is a share of (not drawn as a line); diff: the query subtracted from the others (drawn as the zero line).

focus.description: Series over time: the query key drawn in sky (default: the first query); the others are greys. Two snapshots: a row code to emphasise (LU).

facet.description: Small multiples: one small chart per series (2 to 6), on one shared scale, with the other series as faint context.

align.description: month: monthly series of different years on one January-to-December axis (2025 against 2024, month by month). Default time.

balance.description: Exports against imports: shade the gap between the two series and read out the balance (exports minus imports). Needs exactly two series, flow EXPORT and flow IMPORT, in absolute mode.

sort.description: Two snapshots: rows by b (default), by a, or by the size of the change.

field.description: A field of the rows a query returns (rca, growth, value, share).

options.description: Rendering hints, scalars or short lists of strings. Known: x, y (response fields), format (see format), orientation (horizontal|vertical), limit (rows shown), exclude_codes, reference (a value drawn as a tick, e.g. 1 for RCA), gap_fill (line: shade between two series), highlight_focus (bar: emphasise the is_focus row), center_label (flow), columns (table). 1.1: limit (waterfall: steps shown, default 8; bump: lines; butterfly: rows; treemap: tiles), show_other (waterfall: a step for everything not shown, so the bars add up; default true), measure (choropleth: share|balance|value, default share; 1.7, bar: growth, the growth per year since start from /insights/trends), extent (choropleth, flowmap: world|europe, default europe), flow (flowmap: imports|exports|both, default both), kind (heatmap, required: month_year|product_year|seasonal), scale (heatmap: value|deviation, default value), size (scatter: the bubble field; x and y are required on a scatter), labels (scatter, bump: codes to label), log_x, log_y (scatter), reference_x, reference_y (scatter: a rule, e.g. 1 for RCA, 0 for growth).

story_n.description: Optional (contract 1.6), set by the backend: the page number of the mark's storyline, the [n] of the chat and the circle on the chart. Every mark of a storyline carries the same one; it stays while the storyline is on the page and is never given to another storyline.

target.description: The panel the mark is drawn on.

series.description: Key of one of the target panel's queries (exports, imports).

note.description: What the agent says about the mark, shown in the panel next to its number. Figures only through {fact}.

query.description: Where the mark's own shape comes from: required for trend (/insights/trend) and forecast (/insights/forecast).

status.description: proposed until the user keeps it; clear never removes kept marks.

thread.description: Storyline group: marks that share it are one numbered note on the page.

period.description: The year or month the mark is about. The page dims a mark whose period does not match spec.context.period (a year matches its months). Leave it out for marks about a span or the whole series.

params_thread.description: One path through the crossroads: bought from in_code, sold to out_code, optionally for one product.

params_event.description: A dated rule (a span when until is given).

scenarios.description: Since 1.3: also draw the response's scenarios (for example 'the smartphone line stops / continues') as labelled points at the end of the band. Default false.

params_annotation.description: A leader line to the panel's own data point at x. The y is read from the data by the renderer and is never given.

x.description: A period on a line (2020, 2020-03) or a row code on a bar (FR, 85).

params_highlight.description: codes: bars, Sankey nodes, table rows, countries (choropleth, flowmap), tiles (treemap), rows (butterfly, bump) or bubbles (scatter); from/to: a span on a line.

params_trend_break.description: A lasting shift in a series' level (a change point of /trends/analyze) at a period. before and after name facts of the mark that hold the level on each side (changepoints.[period=2009-01].before_mean); the renderer draws them as two level lines, from 'from' to 'at' and from 'at' to 'to' (default: 6 periods each side).
